Era II

The year is 2016.

You're beginning to hear about AI — and still feeling the burn from CAD.

Era II

2016: the first large-scale push — and a surge of optimism.

The Digital Mammography DREAM Challenge was the first large-scale effort to build breast-cancer AI — and we took part. The hope was that a crowdsourced competition would simply solve it.

1,000+ participants · 126 teams · 44 countries
~640,000 mammograms

Best model AUC 0.858 → ensemble 0.895 → ensemble + a radiologist 0.942. The winner, Therapixel, spun out MammoScreen — still in clinical use today.

Schaffter et al., JAMA Network Open 2020;3(3):e200265.

Era II

2020: Google publishes its breast-cancer AI model.

McKinney et al., Nature 2020 (Google Health, UK + US) — a deep-learning system read screening mammograms stand-alone.

false positives −5.7% US / −1.2% UK
false negatives −9.4% US / −2.7% UK
AUC +11.5% vs avg radiologist
2nd-reader workload −88%

Results are promising — but again, only on clean, curated data.

Era II

2020: three commercial models, independently validated on 8,800 women.

Salim et al., JAMA Oncology 2020 tested three commercial algorithms on an external Stockholm cohort.

best (Algorithm 1) AUC 0.956
AI + first reader 88.6% sens @ 93% spec
exceeded two human readers

Three vendors, external data — the evidence is looking good.

Era II

2026: MASAI interval-cancer result.

~105,000 women. A triage design: high-risk exams → standard double reading; low-risk → a single radiologist.

interval-cancer rate — non-inferior (ratio 0.88)

Gommers et al. (…Lång), Lancet 2026;407(10527):505–514
Era II

2026: the averages look strong — so where do these models still fail?

Overall AUC 0.91 — but performance depends on the imaging feature. Masses, asymmetries, and calcifications are correctly called negative in 60–81% of exams; architectural distortions behave erratically — even screen-detected cancers split bimodally, and many benign distortions score high.

Era II

Data isn't enough to drive adoption.

Enriched cases, lab conditions, no real workflow — CAD had good numbers too. The bar is prospective deployment, and real-world uptake has been slow.
